sections.title: Quick answer

body: The four letters describe direction of attention and energy, what carries weight when taking in information, what criteria carry weight in decisions and how someone approaches the outside world. The convention used here writes ENTP as dominant extraverted Intuition (Ne), auxiliary introverted Thinking (Ti), tertiary Feeling written as Fe and inferior introverted Sensing (Si). The Foundation lists Fe or Fi for tertiary Feeling. The A/T suffix does not change the stack.

The second layer is the Identity that NERIS sets outside the four letters: A and T are the two ends of this dimension, describing the default landing point of self-assessment and sensitivity to pressure. It describes no ability and measures no quality of judgement, and it rewrites none of E, N, T or P. The official MBTI uses four letters only and has no such layer.

In a fictional review, a manager tells two colleagues, “This proposal doesn’t hold up.” Both have the same plan, cost sheet and responsibility. Both ask whether the concern is with the cost estimate or the growth assumption and check which version the manager read.

After the same check, one may still feel sure of most of the reasoning. The other may feel less confident about the argument as a whole. A change in confidence does not show whether the reasoning was sound.

Do not settle your end from one action, one order of events or one first thought. To understand the ENTP orientation and function order, read the [ENTP profile](/en/personality/entp); the original definitions of the two ends are in [the NERIS account](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory), where Assertive is the end that trusts its judgement more and Turbulent the end that doubts itself more readily.
sections.title: ENTP-A and ENTP-T: shared ground and core differences

body: The five rows follow the same fictional review and describe how confidence and pressure might feel at different points. They are reflection prompts, not five components of the NERIS scale.
Both people have the same plan, data, responsibilities and meeting time. In a real review, differences in authority, workload or preparation can change how the feedback feels.
Each row holds the action constant. The final two columns describe possible differences in experience after the same check or feedback.

| Point in the review | What both do | ENTP-A (Assertive) may feel | ENTP-T (Turbulent) may feel |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hearing the same rejection | Ask whether it concerns the cost estimate or the growth assumption. | Still sure of much of the original reasoning. | Less sure of the original reasoning. |
| Hearing the same reason | Record the manager’s reason. | Relatively calm about the challenge. | More unsettled by the challenge. |
| Revisiting the same feedback the next day | Check the same cost sheet and read the same response. | Reassured by the evidence they now have. | Still doubtful about the original judgment despite the same evidence. |
| Checking the same cost assumption | Compare it with the same source data. | Still confident in how they reached the judgment. | Less confident in how they reached it. |
| Reviewing the same proposal that did not pass | Record the correction and what remains uncertain. | More inclined to see the outcome as specific to this proposal. | More inclined to question their judgment beyond this proposal. |

If the data is out of date, check the current data regardless of how the feedback feels. The evidence and deadline determine whether the plan needs to change. The feelings in the table cannot establish a suffix.
sections.title: ENTP-A and ENTP-T: the one-minute comparison

body: How the two handle the same task is clearer from the material and the responsibility. This section uses workplace scenes only to review self-assessment and pressure at the time; it is not for judging who is more reliable, and it does not say who suits which kind of work.
### ENTP-A and ENTP-T facing the same rejection
(Editorial fiction) Both are in the same review, presenting the same plan, holding the same cost data, leaving at the same time and carrying the same responsibility.

In this fictional review, both colleagues ask which assumption the manager challenged, check the same figures and reach the same conclusion. One may still trust the original reasoning and see the problem as a gap in evidence. The other may feel less sure about the reasoning more broadly. Either person can reach the same decision about the plan.
### ENTP-A and ENTP-T told to change direction
(Editorial fiction) The next day the manager requires the plan to move from "build it" to "buy it"; both open the same cost sheet and both have to recalculate on the same timeline.

In this fictional review, both colleagues check the new requirement and recalculate with the same cost figures. One may still feel confident about the decision made with yesterday’s information. The other may feel less sure about it. The new figures, deadline and decision authority determine whether they can propose an alternative.
sections.title: ENTP-A and ENTP-T: work scenes

body: The most common misreading reads A as strong and T as fragile. In NERIS these words mark the default landing point of self-assessment and sensitivity to pressure; they are not a resilience score and do not measure whether a judgement is right.

To compare the two ends, do not compare who keeps their composure better; go back to the record of that review — the plan version, the cost sheet, the exact words of the rejection, the material added afterwards. Who checked what is visible in the material; record the subjective pressure separately and do not use it as evidence about ability.

People also assume the suffix is a fifth position for the four letters, or an official fifth letter. The second letter of ENTP is N and the third is T, and one more letter rewrites neither; the segment after the hyphen belongs to another framework, sits alongside the four preferences, does not stack on them and takes no part in scoring the letters.

One performance is still less of a conclusion. If two results fall on different ends, confirm first whether the tool, the item language and the scoring rules were the same; if the report provides continuous scores, see whether both sit near the A/T boundary. Recent pressure or the experience you were thinking of while answering may affect the answers, but two results alone cannot establish the cause. An inconsistent measurement convention and a different answering situation are two different things: the first has to be unified before comparing, and the second can be recorded as the situation, without abandoning the comparison.
sections.title: ENTP-A and ENTP-T: misreadings to avoid

body: Use the following prompts to reflect on your confidence and pressure after feedback. They cannot establish your suffix or tell you which job fits.

When an argument is rebutted, write down separately the specific objection, which evidence would need adding, and how much confidence remains in the original judgement. Both people can add evidence the same way, and their self-assessment afterwards may still differ. After changing teams or rushing a milestone, observe again; a single reaction cannot settle the end.

To leave a record you can look back on, run a small experiment: next time a plan is rejected, within ten minutes record two things — your confidence in the original judgement and your level of tension — each scored from zero to ten; then record both again after hearing the specific reasons. Looking back a week later at how the two scores moved carries more information than asking what your first reaction was.

Give the experiment a stopping condition: if the recording itself makes you reproach yourself repeatedly, or starts affecting sleep or work, stop; it should not become another self-assessment test. Persistent insomnia or low mood calls for professional support rather than more searching for a cause in a label.
sections.title: ENTP-A and ENTP-T: how to keep observing

body: **Framework sources.** The definitions of the two ends follow [the 16Personalities account of NERIS](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory) and the [dedicated Identity page](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/identity-assertive-vs-turbulent); the four letters follow the [Foundation's type dynamics table](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-overview/).

**Function stack convention.** This page uses Ne–Ti–Fe–Si for both codes. The Foundation lists Fe or Fi for tertiary Feeling. The stack describes type dynamics and does not predict debating skill, task order or an A/T result.

**Editorial fiction statement.** The review where a manager dismisses the plan with "this direction does not hold", the next day's requirement to move from building to buying, the friend saying "I just wanted you to hear me out", and the scoring experiment in the observation record are all editorial fiction used for practice in telling descriptions apart; the descriptions of confidence and pressure are examples, not measurements of anyone.

**Scope limits.** The four-letter sample distribution of MBTI Form M cannot be used to estimate how many people sit at either NERIS A/T end. A result should be read together with the answering environment and recent experience; it is not for hiring screening, relationship prediction or ranking ability, health and safety matters follow professional guidance, and clinical judgement belongs to a qualified professional. For the assessment method, see the [scoring and evidence notes](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types#method-and-evidence).

comparison_public_projection_v1.description: ENTP-A and ENTP-T share the same four preferences. Compare how 16Personalities describes confidence and stress after the same feedback.

faq.answer:
16Personalities separates the two ends on the Identity dimension in NERIS: the A end generally trusts its own judgement more and is less disturbed under pressure; the T end generally doubts itself more readily and is more sensitive to pressure. These are two ends of one dimension, not a fifth official MBTI dimension.

After the same proposal is rejected, both people may verify the same figures and make the same correction. One may feel relatively reassured. The other may feel more doubtful about the earlier judgment. The correction itself cannot tell you which suffix either person received.
faq.question: What is the main difference between ENTP-A and ENTP-T?

faq.answer:
No. Both A and T come from the NERIS suffix system; the official MBTI expresses type with four letters only and has no place for A or T.

Separate the positions: the T in third place covers the basis of judgement, and the character after the hyphen covers self-assessment and response to pressure, which are not the same thing. When a report arrives, look first for a section explaining what A and T each measure and whether the scoring matches the four letters, then decide how to read them together.
faq.question: Are ENTP-A and ENTP-T two kinds of ENTP in official MBTI?

faq.answer:
The suffix measures neither eloquence nor argumentative skill, and A/T cannot be used to infer who argues better. Either end may hear the other's point clearly, and either may change position when the other is right.

Two people can address the same counterexample and differ in how confident they feel about their original argument. To assess the argument, check the evidence and whether the conclusion follows from it.
faq.question: Which one argues better?

faq.answer:
A/T alone cannot determine who errs more easily. Errors relate more directly to task difficulty, whether the material is complete, the time limit and the review process.

Either end may miss an unstated constraint while rushing, and either may miss the moment to speak while checking repeatedly; neither case belongs to one end. To review it, record three things: what information was in hand, how much time was left, and which items were checked in the end, then write down the actual result.
faq.question: Which one is more likely to make mistakes under pressure?

faq.answer:
Division of labour depends on information, authority and available time, not on the suffix, and either end can take either role.

If the two really are to work together, write two things on one page first: who makes the final call, and which data each version of the plan rests on. With those clear, either end can pick up either part; without them, both ends stall waiting for a firm answer. This is collaboration design and has nothing to do with Identity.
faq.question: How would ENTP-A and ENTP-T divide the same job?

faq.answer:
The difference is more likely in self-assessment and pressure when feedback arrives, not in whether someone asks first or stays silent. When a friend says "I just wanted you to hear me out", either end may keep asking questions, and either may stop and listen.

Afterwards you can recall whether you simply felt you had chosen the wrong topic, or read one piece of feedback as failing even at communication. To decide how to respond next time, ask directly whether the other person wants to be heard, wants to discuss options, or wants one fact checked; the three needs call for different responses.
faq.question: How do they differ in a relationship?

faq.answer:
It is possible, but it does not mean the personality changed, and two results alone cannot establish the cause.

Confirm first whether the two results used the same item bank, item language and scoring rules, then check whether the report explains the suffix separately. If it provides continuous scores, see whether both sit near the A/T boundary. Record the situation at each sitting, such as the pressure at the time or the most recent rejection, as clues for understanding the difference, without retesting repeatedly for an "accurate answer".
faq.question: I tested as ENTP-A and later as ENTP-T. Is that normal?

faq.answer:
It depends on whether you are missing the four-letter base or the detail of one end.

This page only compares the two ends, and the four preferences are on the base page. For the base, read the [ENTP profile](/en/personality/entp); for one end alone, read [ENTP-A](/en/personality/entp-a) or [ENTP-T](/en/personality/entp-t).

body: ENTP-A and ENTP-T share Extraversion, Intuition, Thinking and Perceiving. In 16Personalities’ NERIS Identity framework, Assertive (-A) describes greater self-assurance and less sensitivity to stress, while Turbulent (-T) describes greater self-doubt and sensitivity to stress. The official MBTI does not include these suffixes.

Two people can hear the same objection, check the same cost data and make the same correction. They may still feel differently about the judgment they made before the review. The suffix describes confidence and pressure, separate from the quality of the argument.
The T in ENTP stands for Thinking. The -T in ENTP-T stands for Turbulent. Neither a single reaction nor the order of checks can identify someone’s suffix.
sections.title: Quick answer

body: The four letters describe direction of attention and energy, what carries weight when taking in information, what criteria carry weight in decisions and how someone approaches the outside world. The convention used here writes ENTP as dominant extraverted Intuition (Ne), auxiliary introverted Thinking (Ti), tertiary Feeling written as Fe and inferior introverted Sensing (Si). The Foundation lists Fe or Fi for tertiary Feeling. The A/T suffix does not change the stack.

The second layer is the Identity that NERIS sets outside the four letters: A and T are the two ends of this dimension, describing the default landing point of self-assessment and sensitivity to pressure. It describes no ability and measures no quality of judgement, and it rewrites none of E, N, T or P. The official MBTI uses four letters only and has no such layer.

In a fictional review, a manager tells two colleagues, “This proposal doesn’t hold up.” Both have the same plan, cost sheet and responsibility. Both ask whether the concern is with the cost estimate or the growth assumption and check which version the manager read.

After the same check, one may still feel sure of most of the reasoning. The other may feel less confident about the argument as a whole. A change in confidence does not show whether the reasoning was sound.

Do not settle your end from one action, one order of events or one first thought. To understand the ENTP orientation and function order, read the [ENTP profile](/en/personality/entp); the original definitions of the two ends are in [the NERIS account](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory), where Assertive is the end that trusts its judgement more and Turbulent the end that doubts itself more readily.

body: The five rows follow the same fictional review and describe how confidence and pressure might feel at different points. They are reflection prompts, not five components of the NERIS scale.
Both people have the same plan, data, responsibilities and meeting time. In a real review, differences in authority, workload or preparation can change how the feedback feels.
Each row holds the action constant. The final two columns describe possible differences in experience after the same check or feedback.

| Point in the review | What both do | ENTP-A (Assertive) may feel | ENTP-T (Turbulent) may feel |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hearing the same rejection | Ask whether it concerns the cost estimate or the growth assumption. | Still sure of much of the original reasoning. | Less sure of the original reasoning. |
| Hearing the same reason | Record the manager’s reason. | Relatively calm about the challenge. | More unsettled by the challenge. |
| Revisiting the same feedback the next day | Check the same cost sheet and read the same response. | Reassured by the evidence they now have. | Still doubtful about the original judgment despite the same evidence. |
| Checking the same cost assumption | Compare it with the same source data. | Still confident in how they reached the judgment. | Less confident in how they reached it. |
| Reviewing the same proposal that did not pass | Record the correction and what remains uncertain. | More inclined to see the outcome as specific to this proposal. | More inclined to question their judgment beyond this proposal. |

If the data is out of date, check the current data regardless of how the feedback feels. The evidence and deadline determine whether the plan needs to change. The feelings in the table cannot establish a suffix.

body: How the two handle the same task is clearer from the material and the responsibility. This section uses workplace scenes only to review self-assessment and pressure at the time; it is not for judging who is more reliable, and it does not say who suits which kind of work.
### ENTP-A and ENTP-T facing the same rejection
(Editorial fiction) Both are in the same review, presenting the same plan, holding the same cost data, leaving at the same time and carrying the same responsibility.

In this fictional review, both colleagues ask which assumption the manager challenged, check the same figures and reach the same conclusion. One may still trust the original reasoning and see the problem as a gap in evidence. The other may feel less sure about the reasoning more broadly. Either person can reach the same decision about the plan.
### ENTP-A and ENTP-T told to change direction
(Editorial fiction) The next day the manager requires the plan to move from "build it" to "buy it"; both open the same cost sheet and both have to recalculate on the same timeline.

In this fictional review, both colleagues check the new requirement and recalculate with the same cost figures. One may still feel confident about the decision made with yesterday’s information. The other may feel less sure about it. The new figures, deadline and decision authority determine whether they can propose an alternative.

body: The most common misreading reads A as strong and T as fragile. In NERIS these words mark the default landing point of self-assessment and sensitivity to pressure; they are not a resilience score and do not measure whether a judgement is right.

To compare the two ends, do not compare who keeps their composure better; go back to the record of that review — the plan version, the cost sheet, the exact words of the rejection, the material added afterwards. Who checked what is visible in the material; record the subjective pressure separately and do not use it as evidence about ability.

People also assume the suffix is a fifth position for the four letters, or an official fifth letter. The second letter of ENTP is N and the third is T, and one more letter rewrites neither; the segment after the hyphen belongs to another framework, sits alongside the four preferences, does not stack on them and takes no part in scoring the letters.

One performance is still less of a conclusion. If two results fall on different ends, confirm first whether the tool, the item language and the scoring rules were the same; if the report provides continuous scores, see whether both sit near the A/T boundary. Recent pressure or the experience you were thinking of while answering may affect the answers, but two results alone cannot establish the cause. An inconsistent measurement convention and a different answering situation are two different things: the first has to be unified before comparing, and the second can be recorded as the situation, without abandoning the comparison.
sections.title: ENTP-A and ENTP-T: misreadings to avoid

body: Use the following prompts to reflect on your confidence and pressure after feedback. They cannot establish your suffix or tell you which job fits.

When an argument is rebutted, write down separately the specific objection, which evidence would need adding, and how much confidence remains in the original judgement. Both people can add evidence the same way, and their self-assessment afterwards may still differ. After changing teams or rushing a milestone, observe again; a single reaction cannot settle the end.

To leave a record you can look back on, run a small experiment: next time a plan is rejected, within ten minutes record two things — your confidence in the original judgement and your level of tension — each scored from zero to ten; then record both again after hearing the specific reasons. Looking back a week later at how the two scores moved carries more information than asking what your first reaction was.

Give the experiment a stopping condition: if the recording itself makes you reproach yourself repeatedly, or starts affecting sleep or work, stop; it should not become another self-assessment test. Persistent insomnia or low mood calls for professional support rather than more searching for a cause in a label.
sections.title: ENTP-A and ENTP-T: how to keep observing

body: **Framework sources.** The definitions of the two ends follow [the 16Personalities account of NERIS](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory) and the [dedicated Identity page](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/identity-assertive-vs-turbulent); the four letters follow the [Foundation's type dynamics table](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-overview/).

**Function stack convention.** This page uses Ne–Ti–Fe–Si for both codes. The Foundation lists Fe or Fi for tertiary Feeling. The stack describes type dynamics and does not predict debating skill, task order or an A/T result.

**Editorial fiction statement.** The review where a manager dismisses the plan with "this direction does not hold", the next day's requirement to move from building to buying, the friend saying "I just wanted you to hear me out", and the scoring experiment in the observation record are all editorial fiction used for practice in telling descriptions apart; the descriptions of confidence and pressure are examples, not measurements of anyone.

**Scope limits.** The four-letter sample distribution of MBTI Form M cannot be used to estimate how many people sit at either NERIS A/T end. A result should be read together with the answering environment and recent experience; it is not for hiring screening, relationship prediction or ranking ability, health and safety matters follow professional guidance, and clinical judgement belongs to a qualified professional. For the assessment method, see the [scoring and evidence notes](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types#method-and-evidence).

If the two really are to work together, write two things on one page first: who makes the final call, and which data each version of the plan rests on. With those clear, either end can pick up either part; without them, both ends stall waiting for a firm answer. This is collaboration design and has nothing to do with Identity.
items.question: How would ENTP-A and ENTP-T divide the same job?

items.answer:
The difference is more likely in self-assessment and pressure when feedback arrives, not in whether someone asks first or stays silent. When a friend says "I just wanted you to hear me out", either end may keep asking questions, and either may stop and listen.

Afterwards you can recall whether you simply felt you had chosen the wrong topic, or read one piece of feedback as failing even at communication. To decide how to respond next time, ask directly whether the other person wants to be heard, wants to discuss options, or wants one fact checked; the three needs call for different responses.
items.question: How do they differ in a relationship?

items.answer:
It is possible, but it does not mean the personality changed, and two results alone cannot establish the cause.

Confirm first whether the two results used the same item bank, item language and scoring rules, then check whether the report explains the suffix separately. If it provides continuous scores, see whether both sit near the A/T boundary. Record the situation at each sitting, such as the pressure at the time or the most recent rejection, as clues for understanding the difference, without retesting repeatedly for an "accurate answer".
items.question: I tested as ENTP-A and later as ENTP-T. Is that normal?

items.answer:
It depends on whether you are missing the four-letter base or the detail of one end.

This page only compares the two ends, and the four preferences are on the base page. For the base, read the [ENTP profile](/en/personality/entp); for one end alone, read [ENTP-A](/en/personality/entp-a) or [ENTP-T](/en/personality/entp-t).
items.question: What Should I Read Next About ENTP-A or ENTP-T?

sections.title: ENTP-A and ENTP-T: common questions

sections.body_md:
**Framework sources.** The definitions of the two ends follow [the 16Personalities account of NERIS](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory) and the [dedicated Identity page](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/identity-assertive-vs-turbulent); the four letters follow the [Foundation's type dynamics table](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-overview/).

**Function stack convention.** This page uses Ne–Ti–Fe–Si for both codes. The Foundation lists Fe or Fi for tertiary Feeling. The stack describes type dynamics and does not predict debating skill, task order or an A/T result.

**Editorial fiction statement.** The review where a manager dismisses the plan with "this direction does not hold", the next day's requirement to move from building to buying, the friend saying "I just wanted you to hear me out", and the scoring experiment in the observation record are all editorial fiction used for practice in telling descriptions apart; the descriptions of confidence and pressure are examples, not measurements of anyone.

**Scope limits.** The four-letter sample distribution of MBTI Form M cannot be used to estimate how many people sit at either NERIS A/T end. A result should be read together with the answering environment and recent experience; it is not for hiring screening, relationship prediction or ranking ability, health and safety matters follow professional guidance, and clinical judgement belongs to a qualified professional. For the assessment method, see the [scoring and evidence notes](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types#method-and-evidence).
